title: Zero Virtual DOM: Components Run Once as Setup Functions
prerequisites: React rendering model vs SolidJS reactivity

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In React, a component is like a movie projector that replays the entire scene from frame 1 every time an actor blinks. In SolidJS, a component is a construction worker who builds a house once on day 1, attaches live electronic wires to the light switches (signals), and goes home forever. The house never gets rebuilt; only the light bulb turns on and off.
progressiveExplaining.junior: In SolidJS, **component functions execute exactly once** when they are created (mounted). They never re-render. When a signal updates via `setCount()`, the component function does *not* re-run. Instead, only the specific micro-expression or DOM node that called `count()` updates directly. Destructuring props in the function signature (`function App({ count })`) breaks reactivity because the function never re-runs to receive new prop values.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, SolidJS completely eliminates the Virtual DOM and component-level reconciliation. Component functions are purely setup constructors that instantiate reactive graph scopes (owners) and return compiled real DOM nodes. Because there is no render loop, hook dependency arrays (like `useMemo` / `useCallback`) do not exist. Closures, timers, and event listeners declared inside a Solid component run once at creation time, eliminating stale closure bugs.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: The Solid JSX compiler transforms JSX into template cloning instructions: `const _el$ = _tmpl$.cloneNode(true)`. Dynamic expressions inside the template are wrapped in fine-grained computations: `_$insert(_el$, count)`. During the single component execution pass, Solid creates an `Owner` node on the reactive tree. When signals update, only the specific leaf `Computation` attached to `_insert` evaluates, performing a surgical DOM node update (`node.data = val`).

rosettaStone.react: Component function re-runs on every state change; requires `useMemo`/`useCallback`.
rosettaStone.angular: Component class instantiated once; change detection runs template check passes.
rosettaStone.vue: `<script setup>` runs once, but the internal render function re-runs with VNode diffing.
rosettaStone.svelte: Component script runs once; compiler emits surgical update blocks.

codeComparison.title: React Component Re-Render vs SolidJS Run-Once Execution
codeComparison.summary: Console logs in React run on every click; in SolidJS, the component body runs once and only the DOM binding updates.

legacyOrBad.label: React Re-Rendering Component
legacyOrBad.snippet: const [count, setCount] = useState(0); console.log('Rendered'); // ❌ Logs on every click

modernOrGood.label: SolidJS Run-Once Component
modernOrGood.snippet: const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0); console.log('Mounted'); // ✅ Runs ONLY ONCE

interviewGotchas.question: Why is destructuring `props` in a SolidJS component considered an anti-pattern that breaks reactivity?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: This is the #1 gotcha interviewers use to check if a developer understands Solid's execution model.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Because Solid components run **only once**, destructuring `props` in the function parameter (e.g. `function Card({ title })`) extracts the property's raw primitive value at the exact moment of initial setup. When the parent component passes a new `title`, the child component function does not re-run, so `title` remains frozen as its initial value. To preserve reactivity, you must access props via property access `props.title` or use `splitProps(props, [...])`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never write `const { name, age } = props;` in SolidJS. Always use `props.name` or helper utilities like `mergeProps` / `splitProps`.

interviewGotchas.question: Do you need `useCallback` or `useMemo` for event handlers or child components in SolidJS?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Tests understanding of closure creation in non-re-rendering frameworks.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. `useCallback` does not exist in SolidJS because inline functions defined in the component body are instantiated only once during initial mount. They are never re-created on signal updates. `createMemo` exists only to cache expensive derived calculations, not to preserve reference equality across re-renders.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Wrapping simple event handlers or calculations in `createMemo` just for reference stability is completely unnecessary and adds overhead in Solid.
